Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spikes and downstream failures (Nov 12)

Ethan,

Thanks again for taking this — we had a fairly bad incident on Friday (Nov 12) where multiple inference requests started timing out at ~800–1,200ms for ~3 hours during our evening batch window. That spike caused retries in our pipeline and delayed a number of jobs; we estimate ~18% of that night’s pipeline failed and had to be reprocessed.

Our contract references a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for the hosted route. This was the first event of that scale in our account history and it directly impacted our revenue reporting batch. Given the business impact, the procurement team is asking for a remediation package: an account credit and a 30-day extension on our annual contract term to offset the lost processing window while we validate our backfill.

I’ve attached a short incident log from our side (nebula_incident_log_20261112.pdf). Let me know what you can do — ideally a proposal we can present internally by EOD Monday.

— Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Platform Reliability, Nebula Analytics

Sophie — thanks for the detail and the log. I’m really sorry this affected your batch window. I’ve pulled the Redwood side traces and we see a short-lived scheduler/network hiccup in the west-us cluster coincident with your window; it impacted a subset of tenancy and triggered elevated queue times.

I’m looping in Marissa to surface this for an account-level remediation. I think a one-time credit plus a short contract extension (30 days) is reasonable given the impact; I’ll propose numbers below and get exec sign-off.

Proposed preliminary package (subject to approval):
- One-time credit equal to 20% of November usage (applied as account credit)
- 30-day extension to current annual term (no change in pricing)
- 90 days of enhanced monitoring (no additional charge)

I’ve asked our ops team for an internal incident summary and will attach it once ready. Expect a formal proposal from us today.

Thanks for the patience — we want to make this right.

— Ethan
